title: Adic completeness for a finitely generated subideal
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $L\subseteq K\subseteq A$ ideals. Suppose $L$ is finitely generated (there exist $f_1,\ldots,f_r\in A$ with $L=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$) and $A$ is $K$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. Then $A$ is $L$-adically complete.

source.place: Tag 090T (lemma-complete-by-sub), specialization M=A; statement and proof, lines 22776–22806.

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring], $\bigcap_{n\geq1}K^n=0$. Since $L^n\subseteq K^n$, also $\bigcap_{n\geq1}L^n=0$. Thus the canonical map $A\to\varprojlim_nA/L^n$ is injective: an element in its kernel lies in every $L^n$.

Fix $f\in K$ and a compatible family in $\varprojlim_{n\geq1}A/f^nA$. Choose representatives $a_n\in A$. Compatibility gives $a_n-a_{n+1}=f^nz_n$ for some $z_n\in A$. For $m\geq n$, telescoping gives $a_m-a_n\in f^nA\subseteq K^n$. Hence $(a_n\bmod K^n)_n$ is compatible. The bijection defining $K$-adic completeness [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring] gives $x\in A$ with $a_n-x\in K^n$. Write $b_n=a_n-x$; then $b_n\in K^n$ and $b_n-b_{n+1}=f^nz_n$.

source.place: Tag 090T, principal-ideal case through the replacement x_n by x_n-x.

proof.text: For fixed $n\geq1$ put $s_c=\sum_{j=0}^{c-1}f^jz_{n+j}$ for $c\geq1$. If $d\geq c$, then $s_d-s_c\in K^c$, since $f\in K$. Thus $K$-completeness [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring] gives $y_n\in A$ with $y_n-s_c\in K^c$. Telescoping gives $f^ns_c=b_n-b_{n+c}$. Consequently $b_n-f^ny_n=b_{n+c}+f^n(s_c-y_n)\in K^{n+c}$ for every $c\geq1$. Its membership in all powers of $K$ forces $b_n=f^ny_n$. Therefore $a_n-x\in f^nA$ for every $n$, so $A\to\varprojlim_n A/f^nA$ is surjective. This proves the principal case without cancellation of $f$ or any closed-ideal assertion.

source.place: Tag 090T, final displayed tail sum and the two following sentences.

proof.text: Choose the stated finite generators $L=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$. Each $f_i\in K$, so steps 2–3 show that every principal completion map $A\to\varprojlim_nA/f_i^nA$ is surjective. Apply [lem-sfb-adic-surjectivity-from-principal-generators] to these generators: $A\to\varprojlim_nA/L^n$ is surjective. For $r=0$, the same lemma applies with an empty family (and $L=0$). Combine surjectivity with step 1 and the definition [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring] to obtain $L$-adic completeness.
